name: Amlodipine
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 5 mg once daily; maximum 10 mg once daily (2.5 mg start if small, frail, elderly or hepatic insufficiency)

usual_adult_dose.indication: Chronic stable or vasospastic angina; coronary artery disease

key_interactions.effect: Amlodipine 10 mg raised simvastatin exposure by 77%.
key_interactions.action: Do not exceed simvastatin 20 mg daily.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., diltiazem, itraconazole, clarithromycin)
key_interactions.action: Watch for hypotension and edema; reduce the dose if needed.

key_interactions.effect: Higher immunosuppressant levels (cyclosporine trough about +40% in kidney transplant patients; tacrolimus up to 2.5- to 4-fold).
key_interactions.action: Monitor trough levels often and adjust the dose.

common: Edema (dose related: 1.8% at 2.5 mg, 3.0% at 5 mg, 10.8% at 10 mg vs 0.6% placebo)
serious: Worsening angina or acute myocardial infarction on starting or increasing the dose (severe obstructive coronary disease)

monitoring: Cyclosporine or tacrolimus trough levels after starting or changing the dose

pk.half_life_eskd: Not separately reported; PK not significantly influenced by renal impairment (label).
pk.metabolism: Extensive (about 90%) hepatic conversion to inactive metabolites; CYP3A substrate
pk.excretion_renal_pct: 10% as parent and 60% as metabolites in urine
pk.dialyzability: No: highly protein bound; hemodialysis not likely to help (label).
